line.comment: * Task -1.
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: Fixed timers being initialized inside loop rather than outside.
* Merged repair and maintenance timers into one.
* find all fleet leaders and put in $fleetLeaders
* Ensure the Fleet Commander script is on every leader and that all fleet ships are named properly.
* ZH 1.5 local monitoring script on each commander, handles follower scanning range and speed control
* Mordan

* If the player manually adds a ship to an existing fleet, it should auto-hide that new ship and join it to the fleet, which is what Mayhem.Task.TemplateWhenReady does when a new ship is automatically built for a fleet.
* This eliminates the need for the player to go through multiple steps to do this manually.
* Note, that it will only do this once for that ship, which allows the player to manually make the ship visible again if they wish and it will stick.
* Reinforcements.
* ZH 2.0 - automatic ship building features can only fill up half of the outpost construction queue
* Expanded 2.2: Fixed automatic reinforcements exceeding their share (off-by-1 error) of the construction queue.
* Mordan3 - For the sake of fighter reinforcements, the call above does NOT consider carrier support fighters in it's total of fleet ships.
* When new fighters are produced for a fleet with carriers, they are FIRST spread out among the carriers as support fighters (and are thus not direct fleet members)
* So when you instruct reinforcements to keep 10 fighters in a fleet, it would continually add 10 over and over until every carrier filled up in the fleet and only then
* would excess be added to the fleet itself, and only then would this stop making more. Instead, what we want to do is have the reinforcements determine
* the TOTAL ships in a fleet, including all owned support fighters so that this does not overfill the fleet.
* Find all fleet support ships
* for each ship in the fleet, including the Fleet leader, find all support ships and add them to the overall array of $ships.
* does it hold and own other ships?
* add all $owned ships to the cloned ship array
* add those support ships to our $ships array.
* end Mordan3
* basic ship type
* full ship template
* If I still need more of this ship after looking at the backlog,
* Count how many of these specific ships we already have in the fleet
* If I still need to buld more, build them.
* ZH 2.0 - if we cannot afford the full quantity we reduce the order
* at this point we can always afford at least 1 ship
* only ordering the basic ship type
* ordering full ship template
* Monitored sectors.
* Make sure we are strong enough before interrupting our current task, if any.
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: Guard against 0 allied fleet strength.
* ZH 2.0 - dont go if other monitoring fleets are already responding to that sector
* monitoring targets must match exactly
* Expanded 2.2 (ported from FoF): Monitoring claims only an idle fleet.
* A player-issued fleet order is not preempted, and a diversion already under way is not retargeted.
* Retreat and repair.
* ZH 2.0 - presence of hostile freighters no longer blocks repairs
* Retreat from large enemy groups.
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: Fix typo and divide-by-0 error.
* Sector is hot: retreat if necessary.
* Prior to this change, if there were enemies above, the repair/maintenance would never be called. Now we handle it even if there are enemies in local.
* Mordan4
* write to log file 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='%s fleet is evaluating Repairs and Inspection. Inspection threshold: %s', $fleetLeader, $autoInspectionThreshold, null, null, null
* Sector is safe: send to repair damaged ships, or send to inspection if needed.
* NOTE, the fleet leader isn't considered, so if he gets damaged, you're f'd. Maybe we should auto-reassign a new leader, or periodically warn the player.
* if automaintain, and there are no enemies around, check the need for maintenance.
* Mordan4. Check fleet leader for Mantenance and repair, but don't send him anywhere. Instead, just warn the player every 6-10 minutes.
* The code above will not send the fleet leader for maint or repair because it really requires the player to make those decisions manually.
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: Reworked - merged the two timers together. Also, warning is now given every 30min instead of 6-10min.
* end if $autoRepair OR $autoMaintain
* end for each $fleetLeader
* M1 and M2 maintenance is handled manually by the player as this is a more critical decision requiring their consideration.
* Maintenance check for fleet member.
* Mordan4
* write to log file 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='Ship %s needs inspection', $ship, null, null, null, null
* Mordan4
* write to log file 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='Sending ship %s for inspection', $ship, null, null, null, null
* Mordan4. changed repair threshold, so that a fleet member has to fall below that to be sent for repairs automatically.
* M1 and M2 repair is handled manually by the player as this is a more critical decision requiring their consideration.
* Repair check for fleet member
* Support ships have their own system. See Mayhem.Task.Support.
* already being repaired?
* It's already getting an inspection?
* For Renegades, carrier logistics rule. A carrier will automatically repair other fleet ships around it, even if not docked.
* if enemies in system, only go repair if our hull is below 20%. Keep ships in the fight until they go critical.
* no enemies are present, so we repair any ship below 90% hull.
* Mordan4
* write to log file 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='Ship %s needs Repair', $ship, null, null, null, null
* Mordan4
* write to log file 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='Sending ship %s to for outpost repair. It has %s hull', $ship, $ship.hull, null, null, null
